headline: Dhaka and Delhi discussing PM's potential visit to India
summary: Diplomatic sources indicate discussions are underway for a bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Delhi in the third week of August.
details: Diplomatic sources from Dhaka and Delhi report that high-level political contacts are continuing to organize a potential bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India in the third week of August.
The visit, invited by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is currently being discussed at the policy level to finalize the date and key issues to be addressed.
Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi is currently in Delhi, consulting with Indian policymakers to convey Dhaka's message and seek guidance from PM Modi to move the relationship forward.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam stated that bilateral discussions between the heads of government provide opportunities to solve many problems.

The State Minister also emphasized that the people of Bangladesh would not appreciate a convicted prisoner, referring to Sheikh Hasina, speaking from Indian soil, noting that the memories of the July uprising are still fresh.

She added that while the government is positive about visiting all countries, including India and Japan, the final dates depend on the Prime Minister's schedule and the progress of bilateral discussions.
The Prime Minister will not be attending the BRICS outreach session, it has been confirmed.
caption:
Is a high-level diplomatic reset coming? Dhaka and Delhi are in talks for a potential visit by PM Tarique Rahman to India.

Diplomatic sources from Dhaka and Delhi report that high-level political contacts are continuing to organize a potential bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India in the third week of August.

The visit, invited by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is currently being discussed at the policy level to finalize the date and key issues to be addressed.

Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi is currently in Delhi, consulting with Indian policymakers to convey Dhaka's message and seek guidance from PM Modi to move the relationship forward.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam stated that bilateral discussions between the heads of government provide opportunities to solve many problems.

The State Minister also emphasized that the people of Bangladesh would not appreciate a convicted prisoner, referring to Sheikh Hasina, speaking from Indian soil, noting that the memories of the July uprising are still fresh.

She added that while the government is positive about visiting all countries, including India and Japan, the final dates depend on the Prime Minister's schedule and the progress of bilateral discussions.

The Prime Minister will not be attending the BRICS outreach session, it has been confirmed.

headline_marked: Energy crisis deepens as [[Summit LNG supply stops]] due to rough seas
headline: Energy crisis deepens as Summit LNG supply stops due to rough seas
summary: Supply disruptions at the Summit LNG terminal have intensified the national gas shortage, while the Power Minister admits there is no immediate solution to the energy crisis.
details: Gas supply from the Summit LNG terminal has been suspended due to adverse weather and rough seas, forcing the removal of the cargo ship from the terminal.

While the Accelerate Energy LNG terminal continues to supply approximately 190 million cubic feet of gas to the national grid, the loss of Summit's supply has significantly reduced overall availability.
This disruption has worsened an already critical gas shortage, causing long queues and hardships for consumers, including drivers waiting hours for fuel.
Power and Energy Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud stated that the government does not have an immediate solution to the power and energy crisis.

The Minister noted that sustainable improvement will only occur after the implementation of several initiatives, including the construction of more LNG infrastructure and the drilling of new gas wells.
